label: copy-phase input c when the output is also c (late, doubled "cc" in the original)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, only when the fed-back input token is c (100% of activations). About 86% of activations (92% of mass) are at steps where the output is also c, meaning the original sequence has a doubled "c c" pair; the feature fires on the first fed-back c of the pair. It never fires at recall_idx < 3 (t < L+3), and mass leans toward the end of the sequence (to_go 0-1 holds about 72% of mass). The largest activations (up to 1.5) come from short-to-mid sequences ending in "...c c" or "c c x" near the end. Weak residual activations occur on copy-phase c inputs with a different output token. Does not fire in the original phase, on <DEL>, or on any non-c input. Precision is low (~0.3): many structurally identical "cc" copy steps stay inactive, and no simple variable explains which ones fire, so the feature is a sparse, thresholded subset of this context.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: c, -, z, e, i, 2; least: q, 3, d, <DEL>) and the token being output (most: c, i, v, d, 0, x; least: w, u, g, -); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=4, L=5 & t=9, recall_idx=3.
